i1.title: Battery, raw materials, recycling
points: Typical batteries hold 40–90 kWh and lose about 12 % capacity in 300,000 km; warranties run 8–10 years / 150,000–200,000 km (see "Battery & resale").
Switzerland has no raw-material deposits; processing is dominated by China; recycled content stays in the single-digit % until the mid-2040s (BFE/BAFU 2026).

EVs need about 320 Mt of critical-mineral ore, versus more than 100 bn t of fossil fuels extracted in 2024; recycling could cover 10–20 % of lithium/nickel and over 30 % of cobalt demand by 2050 (IEA 2026).

Take-back is free (sestorec, SENS eRecycling, INOBAT); Swiss plants (Batrec, Librec, Kyburz) recover up to 97 % of active materials (company figures); used batteries get a second life as stationary storage.
The EU battery passport applies from 18 Feb 2027; there is no binding Swiss equivalent yet.

i2.title: Front-loaded vs. back-loaded emissions
points: An EV causes most of its emissions in production, a combustion car in operation – driving the old car "to the end" still causes its operating emissions.
A same-size switch saves greenhouse gases in more than 92 % of model combinations (more than 95 % for pure combustion cars).
From about 8,000 km per year switching almost always pays off; below 4,000–5,000 km per year mostly not.
The saving per km does not depend on the current car's mileage (all BFE/INFRAS 2025).

depreciation_curve.ev: BFE/EBP 2023, Figure 2 (Eurotax retail values of EVs, share of new price), ages 1–8 for small and medium cars; large cars use the medium curve; beyond 8 years extrapolated with −20 % per year; ±2 percentage points per 10,000 km above or below 15,000 km a year, at most down to 40 % and up to 125 % of the typical value; the value never rises with time
depreciation_curve.ev_used: used EV bought at age 4: price = new price × value share at that age; its value later = new price × share at age 4 + years kept (so from about 5 years kept the curve is extrapolated)
depreciation_curve.current_car: your value today (or estimate: new price × 0.85 per year of age, minus 1 % of the new price per 10,000 km above 15,000 km a year, at least 5 %); from today −18 % per year (our assumption, close to Eurotax-type curves), plus −2 % per 10,000 km above 15,000 km a year
depreciation_curve.uncertainty: residual value band ±15 % where the EV curve is data, ±30 % where it is extrapolated or beyond 8 years; your car ±20 % (±30 % beyond 8 years)
depreciation_curve.battery: warranty assumed 8 years / 160,000 km (typical, check your offer); replacement scenario CHF 250 per kWh gross capacity (Nissan list prices 2022 via Auto Bild / t-online), shown separately: the residual values are market prices of cars with their original battery and do not include a replacement

email.subject: Request: charging point for my parking space
email.body:
Dear [Name of landlord / property management],

I rent a flat at Vadianstrasse 10, 9000 St. Gallen, parking space [number]. I am planning to switch to an electric car and would like to charge it at my parking space.

I would therefore like to ask for your approval to install a charging point (wallbox) at my parking space, and to discuss the details with you:
1. Which installation do you consider suitable for the building (own connection, existing infrastructure, shared solution)?
2. How would the costs be shared, and would the parking rent change after the installation?
3. Who would arrange the installation, and which technical or legal requirements apply in our building?

A guide by EnergieSchweiz on charging infrastructure in rented buildings, with practical examples, is available here: https://www.energieschweiz.ch/ladeinfrastruktur/werkzeuge/ladeinfrastruktur-in-mietobjekten/

I am happy to discuss this by phone or in person. Thank you for your support.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
[Telephone / email]

subsidies.name: Ladestationen
subsidies.description: Die Stadt St.Gallen fördert die Installation von Ladestationen für Elektrofahrzeuge. Voraussetzung für die Förderung ist, dass die E-Ladestation rund um die Uhr für die öffentliche Nutzung zur Verfügung steht und auf einer öffentlichen Plattform sichtbar ist. Für Elektro-Ladestationen, die Ost-mobil neues Fenster, dem Ostschweizer Netzwerk für E-Mobilität angeschlossen sind,  werden höhere Förderbeiträge ausbezahlt.
subsidies.description_en: The city of St. Gallen funds the installation of charging stations for electric vehicles. The condition for funding is that the e‑charging station is available around the clock for public use and is visible on a public platform. Higher funding contributions are paid for e‑charging stations that are connected to Ost‑mobil's new window, the Eastern Swiss network for e‑mobility.

work.what: Your workplace has parking but no charger yet.

email.subject: Request: charging electric cars at our company parking
email.body:
Dear [Name / HR / Facility Management],

I drive to work by car and park at [address of the company parking]. I am planning to switch to an electric car and would like to be able to charge it at work.

Could you please let me know:
1. Is charging at our company parking already available or planned?
2. If not, would the company be willing to look into installing charging points, and who is the right contact for this?
3. If charging is possible: what charging power (kW) is available, can I charge during the whole working day, and how would the electricity be billed?

I am happy to discuss this in person or to provide more information.
Thank you for looking into this.

Kind regards,
[Your name]

charging_time.home_ac: With a home wallbox (11 kW AC) one overnight session covers several days of typical use: charge 1-2 times per week overnight.
charging_time.public_ac: At a public AC point the car stays several hours, for example overnight or during work.
charging_time.public_dc: Fast charging (DC) takes about 20-30 minutes for a typical weekly need: charge while shopping.

tips: About 514 sites in Switzerland offer high-power charging (150 kW or more).
The operators with the most high-power points are Energie 360 Grad AG, Tesla, Shell Recharge.
Use a charging card or app that works across several networks (roaming) and check its coverage and prices for these operators before you travel.
info_b.source: BFE ich-tanke-strom (charging points with 150 kW or more)

countries.coverage_statement: Good public charging (130 points per 100k inhabitants, 76,511 points in total); balanced AC/DC mix (DC share 24%).
countries.general_tips: Good overall coverage with a solid DC share; autostrada service areas are well equipped. Use a roaming card/app (your Swiss charging card or a multi-network app) and check its coverage and roaming prices for the country before travelling. Bring your own Type 2 cable for AC charging; CCS Combo 2 is the DC standard across Europe. Under AFIR (EU/EEA), newer public fast chargers must accept ad-hoc payment by (contactless) card and show the price per kWh before you start. Plan fast-charge stops on long routes; on TEN-T core corridors pools every 60 km with 150+ kW points are guaranteed.

general_tips: Check that your charging app or card works at the planned stations.
Check the current price and any extra fees before charging.
Plan charging stops along your route and confirm the connector suits your car.
